outcome: No posted result since 26 January 2024 settles, or moves a quantity named in, the structure of Keisler's order. The structural results all predate 2024 (2012 to 2022 first postings; the 2024 journal appearances of the Model Theory, APAL and JSL papers do not change their dates). The only in-window mathematical item is Malliaris's September 2025 expository survey, which restates earlier results and names open questions without settling any. Two August 2026 papers that surfaced in the AI search are outside this bullet: one on Keisler measures (a namesake) and one on the stable forking conjecture (a neighbouring problem); neither mentions Keisler's order.
problem_asks: The bullet asks for the structure of Keisler's order: the preorder on complete countable first-order theories in which T is below T' when every regular ultrafilter that saturates T' also saturates T (Keisler 1967). The statement is loose. Read from the statement alone it asks for: (i) the classes of the order and how the theories are distributed among them, i.e. the full structure of the preorder; (ii) how many classes there are; (iii) whether the order is linear, or what comparability holds between classes; (iv) the minimum class and the maximum class, and a description of each (syntactic or model-theoretic); (v) the dividing lines that separate classes (for example stability, simplicity, lowness, SOP-type properties) and whether they are the boundaries of the classes. The statement names no sub-case and no hypothesis, so ZFC is the default setting. A result that settles one of these parts does not by itself determine the structure, so the parts are kept separate in the events below.

events.what_happened: Maryanthe Malliaris and Saharon Shelah, 'A Dividing Line Within Simple Unstable Theories' (arXiv 1208.2140, submitted 10 Aug 2012; published Adv. Math. 249 (2013) 250-288). Gives the first ZFC dividing line in Keisler's order among unstable theories: for suitable infinite lambda they build a regular ultrafilter D such that ultrapowers of models of stable theories, and of the random graph, are lambda^+-saturated, while ultrapowers of theories that are not simple, or not low, fail to be lambda^+-saturated. Read from the arXiv abstract page.
events.revisions: v1 only (10 Aug 2012); journal version Adv. Math. 249 (2013) 250-288.
events.delivers: A ZFC dividing line within the unstable part of the order, in the simple/low region: one regular ultrafilter saturates the stable and random-graph theories, and fails for non-simple and non-low theories. It locates a boundary; it does not describe every class.
events.remains: Everything beyond that boundary: the internal structure of the simple and low theories, the position of non-low simple theories, and any syntactic description of the classes.

events.what_happened: Malliaris and Shelah, 'Cofinality spectrum theorems in model theory, set theory and general topology' (arXiv 1208.5424, submitted 27 Aug 2012; v2 28 Mar 2015; J. Amer. Math. Soc. 29 (2016) 237-297). The abstract, read on the arXiv page, poses whether SOP2 is maximal in Keisler's order and whether p = t, and says both are translated into a more basic problem which is fully solved by model-theoretic methods. Secondary summaries (a search-result summary of the paper's Theorem 11.11, and Casey and Malliaris's 2017 notes, arXiv 1709.02408, not opened) say the paper proves that every theory with SOP2 is maximal in Keisler's order. I did not read the theorem in the full text.
events.revisions: v1 27 Aug 2012; v2 28 Mar 2015 (editorial and expository changes, per the arXiv comments); journal J. Amer. Math. Soc. 29 (2016) 237-297.
events.delivers: Per the secondary summaries (not checked in the text): every theory with SOP2 is maximal in Keisler's order. This covers the SOP2 theories only and says nothing about theories without SOP2. Its abstract frames the SOP2 question as open before the paper and presents the proof as resolving it.
events.remains: The converse, that SOP2 characterises the maximum class: a conjecture in the companion paper arXiv 1503.08341 (search summary of 1503.08338, not opened), not resolved in any source I read. Also the non-SOP2 part of the order and its minimum-class and linearity structure.

events.what_happened: Malliaris and Shelah, 'Existence of optimal ultrafilters and the fundamental complexity of simple theories' (arXiv 1404.2919, submitted 10 Apr 2014; v2 18 Aug 2015; Adv. Math. 290 (2016) 614-681; report MiSh:1030). Abstract read on the arXiv page: they prove optimal ultrafilters exist on Boolean algebras, which play for simple theories the role that Keisler's good ultrafilters play for all theories; assuming a supercompact cardinal they characterise simple theories by saturation of ultrapowers; and they give a ZFC-level analysis of the global structure of simple theories through the complexity of amalgamation patterns.
events.revisions: v1 10 Apr 2014; v2 18 Aug 2015 (current); journal Adv. Math. 290 (2016) 614-681.
events.delivers: In ZFC: existence of optimal ultrafilters on Boolean algebras, the simple-theory analogue of good ultrafilters. Conditional on a supercompact cardinal: a characterisation of simple theories by saturation of ultrapowers. Restricted to simple theories, and the characterisation needs the large-cardinal hypothesis.
events.remains: An unconditional characterisation of simple theories by saturation; the placement of the non-simple theories; the full order on simple theories, which the abstract describes as having a fundamental complexity with no analogue in stability theory.

events.what_happened: Malliaris and Shelah, 'Keisler's order has infinitely many classes' (arXiv 1503.08341; v1 28 Mar 2015; v2 20 Aug 2015; Israel J. Math. 224 (2018) 189-230). Abstract read on the arXiv page: in ZFC, Keisler's order contains an infinite strictly descending chain of classes of theories, so it is not a well-order. The chain lies inside the simple unstable theories, witnessed by the n-free k-hypergraphs of Hrushovski. Before this paper the order was thought to have finitely many, linearly ordered classes.
events.revisions: v1 28 Mar 2015; v2 20 Aug 2015 (minor edits, updated cross-references); journal Israel J. Math. 224 (2018) 189-230.
events.delivers: In ZFC: the number of classes is infinite, and the order is not a well-order. It shows an infinite descending chain inside the simple unstable theories. It does not give the exact number of classes.
events.remains: The exact number of classes (later settled as continuum many, see malliaris-shelah-2019-not-simple); linearity (see ulrich-2017-nonlinear-supercompact and malliaris-shelah-2018-new-simple-theory); and the full structure.

checked_by.what_they_did: Accepted for publication: Israel J. Math. 224 (2018) 189-230 (read from the arXiv page)

events.direction: Cuts against the older belief that the order is finite and linear, i.e. toward a richer structure. The chain is an explicit ZFC object.
events.object: An infinite strictly descending chain of classes of theories in Keisler's order, built inside the simple unstable theories from the n-free k-hypergraphs (Hrushovski's theories). The abstract does not give the explicit construction; the object is a family of theories with an infinite chain of classes.

events.what_happened: Douglas Ulrich, 'Keisler's Order is Not Linear, Assuming a Supercompact' (arXiv 1702.01237, submitted 4 Feb 2017; one version; 6 pages). Abstract, read on the arXiv page: 'We show that Keisler's order is not linear, assuming the existence of a supercompact cardinal.' A JSL listing for a paper with this title appeared in search results (not opened, so the journal citation is unverified).
events.delivers: Conditional on a supercompact cardinal: Keisler's order is not linear. Says nothing about linearity without that hypothesis.
events.remains: Unconditional (ZFC) linearity; that is addressed by the ZFC incomparability result in malliaris-shelah-2018-new-simple-theory, and the rest of the structure.

events.what_happened: Douglas Ulrich, 'Low is a Dividing Line in Keisler's Order' (arXiv 1704.01537, submitted 5 Apr 2017; one version; DOI 10.48550/arXiv.1704.01537). Abstract, read on the arXiv page, in ZFC: the class of low theories is a dividing line, so that if T is low and T' is Keisler-below T then T' is low; and there is a minimal non-low theory, T_cas.
events.delivers: In ZFC: lowness is downward closed in the order, and there is a least non-low theory T_cas. It establishes one dividing line and one least element above it.
events.remains: The structure of the low theories and of the theories above T_cas, and whether further dividing lines exist. The arXiv abstract does not say.
events.time_since_posted: about 9 years; no journal version identified in my searches
events.direction: Positive for the structure: a ZFC dividing line (lowness) and a least non-low theory.
events.object: The least non-low theory T_cas, a minimal element among the non-low theories in the order. The abstract does not give its definition.

events.what_happened: Malliaris and Shelah, 'An example of a new simple theory' (arXiv 1804.03254; v1 9 Apr 2018; v2 26 Jul 2019; Trends in Set Theory, Contemp. Math. 752 (2020) 121-151; DOI 10.1090/conm/752/15133 per a search result). Abstract, read on the arXiv page: they construct a countable simple theory strictly above the random graph in Keisler's order, though only barely, and in some sense orthogonal to the building blocks of the infinite descending chain. As a result they prove in ZFC that Keisler's order has incomparable classes.
events.revisions: v1 9 Apr 2018; v2 26 Jul 2019 (current); published Contemp. Math. 752 (2020).
events.delivers: In ZFC: incomparable classes exist in Keisler's order, so the order is not linear, witnessed by a countable simple theory strictly above the random graph.
events.remains: Which classes are incomparable in general; the full structure; the simple theories beyond this example.

events.direction: Negative for linearity in ZFC: it proves incomparability, which is stronger than the conditional result of Ulrich 2017.
events.object: A countable simple theory that lies strictly above the random graph in Keisler's order and is, in a sense, orthogonal to the building blocks of the descending chain. Its existence yields incomparable classes in ZFC. The abstract does not give the axioms of the theory.

events.what_happened: Douglas Ulrich, 'Keisler's Order and Full Boolean-Valued Models' (arXiv 1810.05335, submitted 12 Oct 2018; one version; 32 pages; MSC 03C55; no journal listed). Abstract, read on the arXiv page: a compactness theorem for full Boolean-valued models; existence of lambda^+-saturated B-valued models of complete countable theories; and a reformulation of Keisler's order: T0 is below T1 iff for every lambda, every complete Boolean algebra with the lambda^+-chain condition and every ultrafilter on it, saturating T1 implies saturating T0.
events.delivers: A reformulation of Keisler's order in terms of ultrafilters on complete Boolean algebras, plus an existence result for saturated Boolean-valued models. It is a tool, and places no particular theory in the order.
events.remains: All structure claims: the reformulation alone does not settle any class.
events.time_since_posted: about 8 years; no journal version listed; no public engagement found in my searches (not exhaustive)
events.direction: Neutral on which way theories fall: a reformulation.

events.what_happened: Francesco Parente, 'Keisler's order via Boolean ultrapowers' (arXiv 1810.09428; v1 22 Oct 2018; v2 15 Sep 2020; Archive for Mathematical Logic 60 (2021) 425-439; DOI 10.1007/s00153-020-00750-7). Abstract, read on the arXiv page: a new characterisation of Keisler's order by saturation of Boolean ultrapowers, extending the separation-of-variables framework of Malliaris and Shelah; and the statement that good ultrafilters on Boolean algebras are precisely the ones that capture the maximum class in Keisler's order, answering a question of Benda (1974).
events.revisions: v1 22 Oct 2018; v2 15 Sep 2020 (current); journal AML 60 (2021) 425-439.
events.delivers: A characterisation of the order via Boolean ultrapowers, and the ultrafilter condition for the maximum class on Boolean algebras (good Boolean ultrafilters). This describes the maximum class by an ultrafilter condition; it is not a syntactic description of the class, and it does not determine the other classes.
events.remains: A syntactic or model-theoretic description of the maximum class in terms of the theories themselves; the other classes; linearity.

events.what_happened: Douglas Ulrich, 'Amalgamation and Keisler's Order' (arXiv 1811.09902; v1 submitted 24 Nov 2018; v2 last revised 20 Sep 2024; 43 pages; MSC 03C55; no journal listed on arXiv). Abstract, read on the arXiv page: it uniformises the Malliaris-Shelah ultrafilter constructions and sharpens the bounds. Main application: for 3 <= k < aleph_0 and a countable low theory T in which every independent system of countable models can be independently amalgamated, T_{k,k-1} is not below T in Keisler's order; the abstract states this gives T_{k+1,k} not below T_{k'+1,k'} for all k < k'. I did not open v1 or compare the versions.
events.revisions: v1 24 Nov 2018; v2 20 Sep 2024 (in the window; content change relative to v1 not established by me).
events.delivers: Separation within the T_{n,k} family: T_{k+1,k} is not below T_{k'+1,k'} for all k < k' (stated in the abstract as a consequence). The main theorem is about a countable low theory with independent amalgamation; the abstract says the T_{n,k} theories have that property, which I did not check.
events.remains: Comparisons involving theories outside the T_{n,k} family and theories without the amalgamation property; the rest of the structure.
events.time_since_posted: about 8 years for v1; v2 about 2 years ago; no public engagement found in my searches (not exhaustive)
events.doubts: Not established whether the Sept 2024 revision changed the main theorem or its hypotheses compared with v1, which is the scope question the later pass should check. Nothing else in my sources doubts it.
events.direction: Negative for comparability among the T_{n,k} theories: the family does not form a chain at adjacent indices (k+1,k) versus (k'+1,k').

events.what_happened: Malliaris and Shelah, 'Keisler's order is not simple (and simple theories may not be either)' (arXiv 1906.10241; v1 24 Jun 2019; v2 1 Sep 2020; v3 2 Jul 2021; v4 11 Aug 2021; Adv. Math. 392 (2021) 108036, 94 pages). Abstract, read on the arXiv page: Keisler's 1967 order on theories has the maximum number of classes (continuum many) and embeds P(omega)/fin; the witnesses are simple unstable theories with no nontrivial forking, and their growth rates track densities of regular pairs from Szemeredi's regularity lemma. Introduction, read in part through the arXiv HTML: 'Keisler's order has the maximum number of classes, continuum many'; it also mentions unconditional (ZFC) instances of nonlinearity, cited to an earlier paper.
events.revisions: v1 24 Jun 2019; v2 1 Sep 2020; v3 2 Jul 2021; v4 11 Aug 2021 (current); journal Adv. Math. 392 (2021) 108036.
events.delivers: In ZFC: the number of classes in Keisler's order is maximal (continuum many), and the order embeds P(omega)/fin. This settles the count of classes. It does not describe which theories lie in which classes beyond the witnesses.
events.remains: The full structure: which theories lie in which classes, especially among the simple theories, where the paper's own open problems lie (Section 13; not read verbatim, see incomplete); syntactic characterisations of the classes.

events.object: Simple unstable theories with no nontrivial forking, whose ultrapower saturation behaviour is governed by growth rates of hypergraph-type sequences; their existence is what gives continuum many classes. The abstract does not give the explicit theories.

events.what_happened: Malliaris and Shelah, 'Some simple theories from a Boolean algebra point of view' (arXiv 2108.05314; v1 11 Aug 2021; v2 5 Jul 2023; Ann. Pure Appl. Logic 175 (2024), no. 1, part B, Paper 103345). Abstract, read on the arXiv page: separates two families of simple rank-one theories in Keisler's order; T_m (reflecting graph sequences) witness that the order has the maximum number of classes; T_{n,k} are higher-order analogues of the triangle-free random graph; the proof builds Boolean algebras and ultrafilters by hand to satisfy chain conditions. The abstract also says the paper ends with a theorem on flexible ultrafilters and a set of open questions.
events.revisions: v1 11 Aug 2021; v2 5 Jul 2023; journal APAL 175 (2024) (the journal date is 2024, but the first public argument is the 2021 posting).
events.delivers: A separation between the T_m and T_{n,k} families within simple rank-one theories. Restricted to those families; it does not place the other simple theories.
events.remains: How T_{n,k} sits relative to T_m in general; the structure of simple theories beyond these families. The paper's open questions (Question 8.1 on whether one class lies below another, and Question 8.4 on absoluteness, as reported by a search summary) are not verified, because the PDF was unreadable through WebFetch.

It says it extends an idea from the proof that Keisler's order has continuum many classes.

Log. 89(1) (2024) 331-341; DOI 10.1017/jsl.2022.63; first published online by Cambridge University Press 7 Sep 2022). Abstract and Conclusion 1.3, read on the Cambridge page: a Turing functional takes A' to a theory T_A of the complexity of the jump, with A <=_T B iff T_A is below T_B in Keisler's order; Conclusion 1.3 states there is an embedding of the partial order of Turing degrees into Keisler's order. No arXiv preprint was found. The date given is the earliest I found (online-first); an earlier manuscript may exist that I could not find.

events.what_happened: Francesco Parente and Matteo Viale, 'Universality properties of forcing' (arXiv 2310.11691; v1 18 Oct 2023; v2 22 Feb 2025). Abstract, read on the arXiv page: uses forcing to build universal models and studies theories of initial segments of the universe; the results rely on model-theoretic properties of good ultrafilters; a new existence proof for good ultrafilters on Boolean algebras that need not be complete. Keisler's order is not mentioned on the page I read. Included as a borderline event because good ultrafilters define Keisler's maximum class.

events.delivers: An existence result for good ultrafilters on Boolean algebras that need not be complete, and a universality result for forcing. Per the abstract, it does not characterise or move any class of Keisler's order.
events.remains: All structure of the order, per the abstract.
events.time_since_posted: about 3 years; no public engagement found in my searches (not exhaustive)

events.what_happened: Maryanthe Malliaris, 'On ultrafilter construction' (arXiv 2509.14068; one version submitted 17 Sep 2025; math.LO). An expository and personal survey of regular ultrafilter construction and the canonical Boolean algebra developed with Shelah, dedicated to Shelah. Read through the arXiv abstract and HTML passages (partial): it restates that the order has minimum and maximum classes, that the union of the first two classes is the stable theories, that the order is local, that it has continuum many classes (Section 13), and that SOP2 theories lie in three classes (Section 13). Its stated open items are: separating OK and good (Dow 1985, Section 11), and a ZFC version of a Section 12 result 'remains open' (footnote 18). It says the construction programme is part of a book manuscript by Malliaris and Shelah in progress.
events.delivers: No new theorem about the structure of Keisler's order in the parts I read. It restates earlier results: continuum many classes, and SOP2 in three classes. The survey itself presents the canonical Boolean algebra programme; the search summary says it states 'some first theorems' about that algebra, which I did not read verbatim.
events.remains: Everything in the statement. The survey does not claim to settle any part of the structure.
events.time_since_posted: about 13 months (to 11 Oct 2026); no human review or citing work found. The only public description I found was an AI-generated third-party summary page (themoonlight.io), which I did not open and which is not a human reading.
events.doubts: The open items it names concern ultrafilters (OK versus good), not the structure of the order. Its Section 12 footnote states a ZFC question remains open. No doubt about correctness is raised, because it makes no new claim I could find.
events.direction: No direction on the problem: a survey that restates earlier results and lists open items that are not the structure question.

events.what_happened: Gabriel Conant, Kyle Gannon and James E. Hanson, 'Generically stable Keisler measures' (arXiv 2608.24605; v1 25 Aug 2026; v2 16 Sep 2026, whose comment says it 'answers the main question left open in v1'). This is a namesake event, not about Keisler's order: its objects are Keisler measures (Borel-definable global measures on type spaces, in discrete or continuous logic). The abstract, read on the arXiv page, shows that three conditions are equivalent (frequency-interpretation measures; definable measures whose canonical random extension is generically stable; self-averaging measures), and that generically stable measures are closed under Morley products. The abstract states: 'These results are obtained through the use of AI models.' The body names AI systems (see the ai block). The HTML passages I read do not mention Keisler's order.
events.revisions: v1 25 Aug 2026; v2 16 Sep 2026 (comment: answers the main question left open in v1).
events.delivers: Not a result on Keisler's order. It establishes equivalences for generically stable Keisler measures and a Morley-product closure result for them. Under the rule for namesakes it settles nothing about this bullet.
events.remains: The whole of the bullet, unchanged: this event does not bear on it.

Not about Keisler's order: the abstract and page do not mention Keisler, ultrapowers or regular ultrafilters. Recorded as a neighbouring model-theory event found by the AI search. disputes.summary: The conditional nonlinearity result (Keisler's order is not linear under a supercompact cardinal) is attributed to Ulrich (2017). Ulrich's 2018 paper, and a Malliaris-Shelah introduction (read through WebFetch), say the authors and Ulrich independently noticed the supercompact result, and that Malliaris and Shelah later gave ZFC instances. Credit for the conditional result is therefore shared in the literature; I did not establish who had it first.

summary: Searches (about 50 web queries and about 30 page fetches) found no event since 26 January 2024 that settles, or moves a quantity named in, the structure of Keisler's order. Every structural result I could find is dated before 2024: the ZFC dividing lines (2012, 2017 for lowness); SOP2 maximal (first posted 2012, JAMS 2016, per secondary summaries of Theorem 11.11); the infinite descending chain (2015); conditional and ZFC nonlinearity and incomparability (2017 to 2018); the Boolean-ultrapower characterisation of the maximum class (2018, AML 2021); the continuum-many maximum class and embedding of P(omega)/fin (2019, Adv. Math. 2021); the Turing-degree embedding (JSL 2024, first online 2022). Several of these reached journal form during 2024 (Model Theory, APAL, JSL), and two papers were revised in the window (Ulrich 1811.09902 v2, 20 Sep 2024; Parente and Viale 2310.11691 v2, 22 Feb 2025). Under the first-public-argument rule none of these moves a date into the window. The in-window mathematical item is Malliaris's September 2025 survey 2509.14068, which restates earlier results and lists open items about ultrafilters (OK versus good) rather than the structure of the order. The AI search found no AI system credited with anything about Keisler's order. Two August 2026 papers that do credit AI systems are outside this bullet: Conant, Gannon and Hanson's paper on Keisler measures (a namesake, arXiv 2608.24605), and Freitag and Mutchnik's stable forking counterexample (2609.00436), which does not mention Keisler's order. Close calls: (1) whether the September 2024 revision of 1811.09902 changed its main theorem or hypotheses, which I did not establish; (2) the Turing-degree paper has no arXiv preprint I could find, so its first public argument may predate the online-first date of 7 Sep 2022, though either date is before the window; (3) whether the 2019/2021 maximum-classes result, the SOP2 result and Parente's characterisation together 'determine' the structure. The statement asks for the whole structure, and the sources themselves name open questions on the simple theories (Problem 13.1, Question 13.4 in 1906.10241; Questions 8.1 and 8.4 in 2108.05314, as reported in a search summary I could not verify), plus the converse of SOP2 maximality, so I read them as not determined. The AI-search evidence is thin for pre-2024 papers because I read abstracts and metadata, not acknowledgements, for most of them; that is recorded in incomplete.
competing_reading: The strongest case for reading the record differently is that the structure has been largely determined by the 2012 to 2021 series. On that view the order has continuum many classes, is not linear in ZFC, has its minimum class and stable part settled since Keisler and Shelah (1967 to 1978), has its maximum class characterised (SOP2 maximal, and good Boolean ultrafilters), and has proven dividing lines (lowness, simplicity). Then the in-window items are irrelevant, and the problem was largely settled before the window, with nothing left to count. Against this: the bullet asks for the whole structure, the sources themselves describe the simple-theory structure as open, and the SOP2 converse and absoluteness questions are reported as open in the sources I read.
what_would_settle_it: (1) Full-text reading of Section 13 of arXiv 1906.10241 and of the open questions in arXiv 2108.05314 (currently only search summaries). (2) A comparison of v1 and the September 2024 v2 of arXiv 1811.09902, to see whether the main theorem or its hypothesis changed. (3) A direct arXiv listing or full-text search for 'Keisler' in math.LO from January 2024 to October 2026, which my web-search method cannot guarantee to have covered. (4) Reading the full text of arXiv 2509.14068 to confirm it contains no new theorem about the order. (5) The authors' PDF for 2608.24605, to confirm the system quotes given here, which were extracted by WebFetch rather than read directly from the page text.
incomplete: (a) Section 13 of arXiv 1906.10241 (the open problems, including Problem 13.1 and Question 13.4) was not read: the WebFetch extraction stopped at Section 8 in each attempt. The open questions cited here come from a search summary and are unverified. (b) The PDF of arXiv 2108.05314 could not be read through WebFetch (binary output); its Question 8.1 and Question 8.4 are unverified. (c) For most pre-2024 papers I read the arXiv abstract and metadata, not the full text or acknowledgements, so the AI findings for them (none_found true) rest on abstracts and partial HTML, not on full acknowledgement sections. (d) For the Malliaris 2025 survey I read the abstract and partial HTML, not the full text, and I did not read its 'first theorems' on the canonical Boolean algebra verbatim. (e) The system quotes for 2608.24605 were extracted by WebFetch's small model from the authors' HTML, and the ellipses in the extraction mean they are not exact; they need checking against the page. (f) I did not open the Ulrich 2017 JSL listing, the Turing-degree preprint search (none found), the Casey-Malliaris notes (1709.02408), 1503.08338, the AMS JAMS record, Parente's 2019 thesis, the Kingy tracker, the aiweekly and MathWorld pages, or the Gold Rush paper (2608.24961; only a partial table in a search result). (g) The Wikipedia List of unsolved problems in mathematics was read only up to about character 100000 of 294882, and the model-theory section containing the Keisler bullet was not reached, so I did not verify the bullet's wording on the live article; the statement given in the task was used. (h) No arXiv listing or journal index was searched directly; coverage is what the web search returned, and absence of an in-window event is evidence only within that method. (i) No Lean, Coq or mathlib formalisation of Keisler's order was found; I did not browse the mathlib repository directly.

events.ai_basis: A proof of Theorem 1.1 in the discrete case was initially obtained from a ChatGPT 5.5 query.
Using ChatGPT 5.6, we find a counterexample to the stable forking conjecture.

judgement.why: The statement asks for the whole structure of Keisler's order, so every pre-2024 structural result (dividing lines, SOP2 maximality, nonlinearity, continuum many classes, Turing-degree embedding) settles one named part and is a case; the 2015 infinite-chain result only moved the class count and is a bound, superseded by the 2019 continuum result. None is whole, and journal-dated 2024 appearances keep their earlier first-posting dates. The only in-window item on the order itself is Malliaris's 2025 survey, which proves nothing new (none). The two 2026 AI-credited papers concern Keisler measures (a namesake) and the stable forking conjecture (a different problem), so both are variant; their AI roles are recorded from their own quotes but cannot touch this problem.
judgement.doubts: Directions are mostly null because the statement poses no conjecture to confirm or refute; nonlinearity results are marked refuted against the older linear picture. The Sept 2024 v2 of Ulrich 1811.09902 was not compared with v1; nothing suggests new mathematics, so it keeps its 2018 date.
